excerpt: Photo credits: Ron Butler. Nowhere are current cultural, technological, and political changes as visible as in the field of journalism. In many places around the globe, journalists are suffering intimidation, repression, and limitations on press freedom. At the same time, with the rise of social media, journalists have lost their privileged role in our public spheres and now compete with a wide range of other producers of information who may have very different professional backgrounds and intentions. These include influencers, AI chatbots, think tanks, activists, hybrid-warfare specialists, and others. The journalistic business model is also undergoing profound changes, with news and information now available for free and in unprecedented abundance, and with journalism as a paid profession under pressure from AI technologies capable of performing journalistic roles with increasing sophistication. It is easy to be deterred by all this, to think that journalism is not a profession for the future. At the Mundus Journalism programme, we want to counter such scepticism and emphasise that precisely because of these challenges, journalism has never been more important than it is now. The aim of the programme is to give students the analytical skills needed to identify, analyse, and navigate these complex cultural, political, and technological transformations. We believe that a scientifically grounded understanding of these conditions is absolutely crucial to productively developing and rethinking the role of journalism in our societies. We educate our students to be able to take an active part in, and not least shape, this exciting conversation. The courses you take in your first year in Aarhus are designed to provide you with a framework for analysing the social, political, and cultural role of journalism and to prepare you for your specialisation and thesis work in the second year. Below, you will find an overview of the first-year courses to give you a sense of what to expect (keep in mind that some adjustments to course emphasis and content may be necessary due to the fast-paced evolution of journalism and media studies). Introduction to Journalism Studies: Theories and Approaches. Taught by the Department of Media and Journalism Studies, Aarhus University The overall aim of this course is to introduce students to different theoretical and epistemological approaches to understand modern-day news media institutions and journalism practices across the world. Through multidisciplinary perspectives, the course looks at the interrelationship between the news media, journalism, and broader societal processes such as politics, culture, the economy, and technology. In so doing, it introduces students to some of the foundational and emerging theoretical perspectives to understand and interpret contemporary sets of practices, production and reception contexts within which journalism occurs today. Overall, the training throughout this course orients students towards a cross-cultural, critical examination of the legacies and current debates in journalism studies. Throughout the course, students will be trained to apply the different theoretical perspectives in analyses of real-life cases across the world.
